# Rollout Plan: Migrating 40,000 Users from Legacy Billing to New Billing System

## Overview
Both billing systems will run in parallel throughout the migration, allowing rollback of any individual user or cohort without service interruption. Migration proceeds in three phases, moving from low-risk internal validation to full customer-base cutover, with the legacy system kept live and untouched until well after the final user batch has migrated and stabilized.

---

## Phase 1: Canary (Internal & Opt-In Users) — 1% of users (~400 users)

**Entry criteria to start:**
- New billing system has passed end-to-end integration testing in staging, including invoicing, proration, tax calculation, payment retries, and refunds.
- Dual-write/dual-read reconciliation tooling is deployed and verified to detect discrepancies between old and new systems within 15 minutes.
- Rollback procedure for a single user has been tested successfully at least once in staging.
- On-call rotation and escalation path are staffed and documented.

**Scope:** Internal employee accounts, sandbox/test accounts, and volunteer opt-in customers on month-to-month plans (lowest contractual complexity).

**Activities:** Migrate accounts, run parallel billing cycles (both systems compute invoices, only old system's invoice is charged), compare outputs daily.

---

## Phase 2: Early Majority (Segmented Rollout) — 25% of users (~10,000 users)

**Entry criteria to start:**
- Phase 1 ran for a minimum of one full billing cycle (or 30 days, whichever is longer) with zero critical (Sev-1) incidents.
- Invoice discrepancy rate from Phase 1 reconciliation is below 0.1% of invoices.
- All Phase 1 support tickets related to billing have been resolved or triaged with documented root cause.
- Customer support team has been trained on the new system's dashboards and dispute workflows.

**Scope:** Segmented cohorts by plan type and geography (e.g., start with simplest pricing tiers, single-currency regions), expanding in weekly waves of ~2,500–3,000 users. Higher-complexity accounts (multi-currency, enterprise contracts, custom discounts) are deferred to Phase 3.

**Activities:** Continue parallel computation with old system as system of record; begin cutting over actual charging to the new system for stable cohorts after 1 clean billing cycle per wave; maintain daily reconciliation reporting.

---

## Phase 3: General Availability (Full Migration) — 74% of users (~29,600 users)

**Entry criteria to start:**
- Phase 2 cohorts collectively show invoice discrepancy rate below 0.1% and payment failure rate delta versus legacy system below 0.5 percentage points.
- No open Sev-1 or Sev-2 billing incidents in the prior 14 days.
- Finance has reconciled Phase 2 revenue reporting between old and new systems with no unresolved variance greater than 0.5%.
- Support ticket volume per migrated user in Phase 2 is at or below baseline (pre-migration) ticket rate.

**Scope:** All remaining users, migrated in waves by complexity tier (standard accounts first, enterprise/custom-contract accounts last), targeting completion within 8–10 weeks.

**Activities:** Migrate remaining cohorts in weekly waves; new system becomes system of record for each cohort as it completes one clean billing cycle; old system remains fully operational in read/standby mode for all migrated users through at least two full billing cycles post-migration, to support billing history lookups, disputes, and emergency rollback. Decommissioning of the old system is explicitly out of scope for this plan and will be scheduled as a separate, subsequent project only after the full 40,000-user base has been stable on the new system for at least two consecutive billing cycles.

---

## Risks

RISK: Invoice calculation discrepancies between old and new systems (e.g., tax, proration, discounts) leading to over- or under-billing | Run mandatory parallel dual-computation with automated reconciliation for at least one full billing cycle per cohort before cutover; block cutover on any unresolved discrepancy | Billing Engineering Lead
RISK: Payment gateway or tokenization mismatch causes failed or duplicate charges during cutover | Migrate stored payment methods via a tested tokenization bridge in a maintenance window per cohort; freeze new charges for an account during its individual cutover window; monitor duplicate-charge alerts in real time | Payments Platform Owner
RISK: Customer support is overwhelmed by billing disputes and confusion during migration waves | Stagger wave sizes, pre-notify customers by email before their migration date, provide a support runbook and escalation macros, staff extra support capacity during each wave | Customer Support Manager
RISK: Data migration errors corrupt or drop historical billing/invoice records needed for audits or disputes | Migrate historical records as read-only snapshots into the new system with checksums; keep the old system queryable in standby mode for at least two billing cycles post-migration | Data Migration Lead
RISK: Revenue recognition or financial reporting diverges between systems during the dual-running period | Finance performs weekly reconciliation of migrated-cohort revenue between both systems; halt further migration if unresolved variance exceeds threshold | Finance Controller

---

## Halt / Rollback Metrics

The rollout must be immediately paused (no new users migrated to the next wave or phase) if any of the following thresholds are breached for a given wave or phase:

- **Invoice discrepancy rate exceeds 0.5%** of invoices generated by the new system compared to the old system's computation for the same billing period.
- **Payment failure rate for migrated users exceeds legacy baseline by more than 1 percentage point**, sustained over any 24-hour window.
- **Sev-1 billing incident occurs** (e.g., duplicate charges affecting more than 10 customers, or a system outage exceeding 30 minutes).

Any breach triggers an immediate freeze on further migrations, root-cause investigation, and executive sign-off (VP Engineering + Finance Controller) before resuming.

PHASES: 3
